walkthroughs.body_html:
Approaches to Research — a core area of Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Approaches to Research brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Approaches to Research.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Braun and Clarke's 2006 thematic analysis has how many phases?
Reflecting on how the researcher shapes the data is called:
options: Triangulation
Reflexivity
Coding
Saturation

mcqs.q: What is the difference between reliability and validity?
options: Schizophrenia is caused by too much serotonin.
Reliability is consistency; validity is whether it measures what it claims to.
Reliability is for quantitative, validity for qualitative.
They are essentially the same thing.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Focus group”?
options: In-depth investigation of one individual, group or event; e.g. HM (Milner 1957) on memory.
Guided by a topic list; allows flexibility for follow-up while maintaining comparability across participants.
Group interview of 6-10 participants; uses interaction to generate data; risk of dominant voices skewing discussion.
Braun and Clarke (2006) six-phase method: familiarisation, coding, themes, review, define, write-up.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Case study”?
options: Recording behaviour in its natural setting without manipulation; high ecological validity, low control.
In-depth investigation of one individual, group or event; e.g. HM (Milner 1957) on memory.
Researcher reflecting on how their identity and assumptions shape data collection and interpretation.
Guided by a topic list; allows flexibility for follow-up while maintaining comparability across participants.
